title: Utility comparison and target review — working draft
date: September 23,2026 | Research draft prepared before the 10:00 EDT delivery; cluster outcomes not yet collected
summary: The frozen comparison tests a parenthood housing minimum against child-dependent housing expenditure shares, with the same earnings and inherited entry-wealth law within each pair. It can inform utility specification once its numerical and repeat evidence is collected. It does not by itself certify a final calibration.

The target audit supports preserving much of the existing work. It also identifies specific measurement decisions: first-birth housing response, resident versus dependent children, old-age wealth dispersion, bequest coverage, and target population. Several candidate corrections have now been measured, with uncertainty; none has replaced the running targets.

Cluster authentication expired after successful submission. This draft has no fresh job outcomes or selected fits. At the 10:00 delivery the report must use verified collection if available, otherwise explicitly report uncollected results.
recommendations: Keep one persistent earnings process plus the age profile as the working direction and heterogeneous entry wealth as the baseline direction. Do not choose zero wealth to obtain a convenient solution. Numerical resolution and the empirical joint entry law still need separate validation.

Freeze a single measurement contract after the author chooses the quantitative population and first-birth housing-response timing. Implement the empirical and model operators together, preserving all identifying information and stating which coefficients are externally restricted.

Use the proposed common-scale entry construction as a candidate denominator repair. Its scale and current renter budgets are checked against the actual frozen parameters, but its 3-by-5 discretization, age 18–24 proxy, and later household feasibility are not certified.

Compare the utility forms on the complete fit, lifecycle plots, parameter plausibility and repeated numerical solutions. An extra free coordinate in the share model and a lower weighted objective do not establish the right economics or convergence.
limitations: Current objective weights mix sampling uncertainty, across-year variation and an external bequest tolerance. The loss is a working diagnostic distance, not a chi-squared statistic or proof of an efficient SMM estimator.

This draft does not have new selected checkpoints, exact repeats or 17-figure packets. Historical September 22 B calculations used in measurement checks are labeled separately and cannot substitute for new results.

Four-year decision timing, stationary income risk at entry, wealth-grid robustness and finite infeasibility values remain model limitations. Positive current renter slack alone says nothing conclusive about continuation choices.
scientific_verification_status: Not collected. Original-selected versus both repetitions must be verified independently before claiming equality.

sections.title: Exactly what was submitted
paragraphs: 40 production workers:18 per utility with 15-state persistent earnings, plus 2 per utility with 7-by-3 persistent+iid earnings. Each arm has its own two-case smoke, search, two selected repetitions and final comparison. No zero-entry fallback is allowed.

All arms retain inherited heterogeneous entry wealth, the deterministic age profile, current-income purchase eligibility, transfer rules, four-year timing, power equivalence scale, complete target/weight system and 160-node wealth grid with upper 3000. The floor arm estimates 9 structural coordinates; the shares arm estimates 10; fertility utility is normalized separately in every evaluation.

The utility difference is experimental. The floor imposes an additional housing requirement only when children live at home. The alternative removes that requirement and lets the housing share of expenditure rise with current dependents. Both retain the existing equivalence scale. No manuscript specification has been adopted.

paragraphs: There are 12 scored empirical rows plus one separate fertility normalization. Values below remain those used by the frozen experiment. A working scale is the denominator used to turn a moment gap into its loss contribution; the final column states why these scales should not all be called comparable standard errors.

sections.title: First-birth room response: what the replay establishes
paragraphs: One 330-second replay reproduced the original estimate 0.7202463, clustered SE 0.0852601,49,457 observations and 4,112 people. The full 900-by-900 cohort-interaction covariance was recovered. This reproduces the implementation; it does not settle the empirical comparison or its model counterpart.

The following contrasts use common cohorts at both endpoints. The uncertainty conditions on the selected cohort weights. It excludes uncertainty from estimating those weights. The omitted event-2 coefficient is set to zero only for supported reference observations. Different windows and cohort weights are different estimands, not interchangeable robustness numbers.

The current model comparison advances treated and control branches by one four-year step, permitting subsequent births. It is not literally the same regression and cohort weighting. A four-year gap between data endpoints alone is insufficient to establish an exact counterpart.

Codebooks do not support automatically treating the 100 zero-room records as missing: zero denotes a shared-room response. The only surviving raw 98 is in 1991, when 1–98 are allowed counts. This resolves a coding interpretation, not the economic plausibility of 98 rooms. Aggregate census exports completed; a subsequent metadata export failed and is preserved.

Additional saved-covariance calculations give an eight-year -4/+4 contrast of 1.24358 rooms (SE 0.12145; 25 common cohorts, fixed preperiod weights). On the 23 cohorts also observed at -2, the same-weight -4/+4 change is 1.25709, of which 0.39841 (SE 0.10105) occurs between -4 and -2. The remaining -2/+4 contrast is 0.85868 (SE 0.10092). The longer change therefore includes substantial prebirth movement; adopting it solely to bring the target closer to the model would be unjustified.

Opus initially proposed an exact -4/+4 match, then withdrew that claim after the lead challenged its timing assumptions. An explicit model-panel observation rule and matched auxiliary regression are the recommended direction. Uniform birth dates or endpoint/midpoint conventions are sensitivity assumptions, not established timing facts or mathematical bounds. Marginal event-time support does not reproduce full individual interview histories, and education controls cannot simply be dropped only on the model side.

sections.title: Two concrete measurement alternatives
paragraphs: Linked minor children: the ACS family-room gap falls from 0.347067 to 0.336220 rooms when groups use linked children under 18. The paired difference is-0.010847, SE 0.008077 under the same 1,000 metro draws. It is a better candidate for current dependents, but the model departure process still needs a stated age interpretation.

Old-age dispersion: on the exact same PSID sample, p90/p50 of household wealth-to-family-income ratios is 3.515935(SE.306911), whereas p90/p50 of wealth levels is 4.919429(SE.579804). These measure different things. Constant model pensions make the two model ratios coincide; that does not justify using either data number interchangeably.

The national ownership counterpart is 67.626%, above the current 42-metro 64.833% target. A population change therefore does not mechanically fix historical low model ownership. Choose geography from the paper claim, not from the fit.

sections.title: Proposed entry wealth: units checked, equilibrium not run
paragraphs: Use each entrant household's nonhousing net worth divided by the same-wave mean gross earnings of working reference-person households. Unlike division by own earnings, this preserves zero-earnings entrants without imposing an arbitrary denominator floor. The established 18–24 childless-renter sample remains 1,835 family-years/1,346 people, including 67 zero-earnings observations.

The proposed 15 wealth means are formed within 3 earnings terciles and 5 normalized-wealth bins. Actual cell probabilities are retained. Their weighted mean is 0.185775923 model units because mean annual gross working earnings are 1 in the actual frozen parameter object. The native annual return is 2%; working survival is 1, with retirement survival below 1.

An initial postprocessor mistakenly read source defaults rather than the serialized seed. Its 1.112608 conversion and 0.206696 wealth mean are rejected and preserved. The corrected readout uses actual parameters after both frozen utility bindings. No submitted job or inherited entry law was changed.

Inherited unsecured debt can roll over: at age 18 the renter saving floor equals min(b,0). Thus current feasible resources depend on R*b+Y-min(b,0), not R*b+Y alone. All 85 positive node/income pairs and 119 interpolated grid/income points have positive current slack. No Bellman or equilibrium was solved for this candidate.

The 3-by-5 means retain only 20.88% of empirical wealth variance; joint dependence is approximated. The induced weighted rank correlation is.24089, versus.28250 in the empirical rows. Product coupling places.2774% of mass on nine combinations absent from a finer empirical rank-overlap construction. These are disclosed approximation choices, not pass/fail tests.

sections.title: Literature checks and what they do not settle
paragraphs: Kaplan, Mitman and Violante(2020, JPE) discipline initial assets and asset-income correlation empirically, along with aggregate/lifecycle wealth and ownership. This supports measuring entry conditions rather than setting them by convenience; it does not supply a four-year fertility-model entry law for us.

De Nardi and Yang(2014, EER) use the 0.0088 bequest/wealth ratio. The original Gale-Scholz working-paper construction measures transfers to children with spouse-status adjustments and excludes pension/trust wealth. Our model total positive estates need an explicit coverage bridge. Published use alone is not validation of our observer or synthetic 5% tolerance.

Sommer's 2014 FEDS working-paper table targets completed fertility 1.90 and first-birth age 25.5. This illustrates matching the chosen cohort/sample, not a requirement that all models normalize fertility to 2.1. The published JME version was not separately checked here.

Current model normalization pools ages 46+. CPS 40–44 in 2004/2006 gives capped mean 1.856608 and a 3+representative 3.482793, versus inherited 2024 representative 3.602359. Decide population, top-bin representation and timing together. This mismatch alone does not prove the current closure impossible.
